list.label: Contributor
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT contributor FROM whodunit_repos WHERE contributor <> ''

list.name: board
list.label: Board (stage 4)
list.query: SELECT name AS __text, id AS __value FROM boards WHERE id LIKE 'linear:%' ORDER BY name

options.content:
# AI Productivity Funnel
*Six stages, each measured on its own. Adoption is not productivity, and this is laid out so the two cannot be mistaken for each other.*

**The stages do not multiply.** 70% adoption × 80% engagement × 60% assisted work is not a productivity figure — it is arithmetic on unrelated denominators. Each stage validates that the next one is worth asking about; none of them derives the next.

**The units change between stages,** so this is drawn as descending bars rather than a tapering funnel: stages 1–2 count people and sessions, stage 3 counts commits, stage 4 counts issues. A continuous taper would assert that each stage is a subset of the one above it, which is not true here. Every stage shows its own denominator.

panels.title: Adoption funnel — are we adopting AI?
Stage 1 · Adoption

targets.rawSql:
SELECT 'contributors using an agent' AS `stage`,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN e.repo_id IS NOT NULL THEN r.contributor END) AS `value`
FROM whodunit_repos r
LEFT JOIN whodunit_events e ON e.repo_id = r.repo_id AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
WHERE r.contributor <> '' AND ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '$contributor')
UNION ALL
SELECT 'contributors seen at all',
       COUNT(DISTINCT r.contributor)
FROM whodunit_repos r WHERE r.contributor <> '' AND ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '$contributor')

panels.description: Anyone with recorded agent activity, over everyone whodunit has seen commit. Both counts are shown because a percentage from one contributor is noise — the denominator is what makes that obvious.

panels.title: Stage 2 · Engagement — how deep, not how many

targets.rawSql:
SELECT CASE
         WHEN s.mcp_calls > 0 OR s.distinct_tools >= 5 THEN 'agentic — MCP or many tools'
         WHEN s.tool_calls >= 50 THEN 'multi-file work'
         WHEN s.tool_calls >= 10 THEN 'wrote code'
         WHEN s.tool_calls > 0   THEN 'light edits'
         ELSE 'conversation only — no edits'
       END AS `intensity`,
       COUNT(*) AS `sessions`
FROM whodunit_sessions s JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = s.repo_id
WHERE s.last_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000 AND ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '$contributor')
GROUP BY `intensity` ORDER BY `sessions` DESC

panels.description: The panel that adoption hides. A session where the agent only answered questions and a session where it wrote across a dozen files both count as 'used AI'. Weighting by what the agent actually did separates 'people have it open' from 'it is doing engineering work'.

panels.title: Habitual use (WAU / MAU)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ROUND(
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM whodunit_sessions s JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=s.repo_id
   WHERE s.last_seen >= (UNIX_TIMESTAMP() - 7*86400) * 1000000000 AND ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '$contributor')) * 100.0
  / NULLIF((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM whodunit_sessions s JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id=s.repo_id
   WHERE s.last_seen >= (UNIX_TIMESTAMP() - 30*86400) * 1000000000 AND ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '$contributor')), 0), 0) AS v

panels.description: Weekly sessions as a share of monthly. High means the agent is part of the routine rather than something tried once.

panels.title: Sessions doing real work

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(s.tool_calls > 0) * 100.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 0) AS v
FROM whodunit_sessions s JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = s.repo_id
WHERE s.last_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000 AND ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '$contributor')

panels.description: Share of sessions where the agent edited at least one file. The rest were conversation.

panels.title: Value funnel — is AI producing value?
Stage 3 · AI-assisted work

targets.rawSql:
SELECT 'agent lines survived to the commit' AS `stage`,
       SUM(c.method = 'intersected') AS `commits`
FROM whodunit_commits c JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = c.repo_id
WHERE 1=1 AND ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '$contributor') AND c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
UNION ALL
SELECT 'carries an attribution trailer',
       SUM(c.status = 'assisted')
FROM whodunit_commits c JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = c.repo_id
WHERE 1=1 AND ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '$contributor') AND c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
UNION ALL
SELECT 'commits in range',
       COUNT(*)
FROM whodunit_commits c JOIN whodunit_repos r ON r.repo_id = c.repo_id
WHERE 1=1 AND ('$contributor' = '__all__' OR r.contributor = '$contributor') AND c.committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000

panels.description: The one stage of the value funnel with data. Note the split between the middle and top bars: a trailer says the agent worked on the commit, `intersected` says its exact lines were still there when the commit was made.

panels.title: Stage 4 · Cycle time — assisted vs not

targets.rawSql:
SELECT CASE WHEN ai = 1 THEN 'AI-assisted' ELSE 'not assisted' END AS `group`,
       ROUND(AVG(ltm)/60, 1) AS `hours`
FROM (
  SELECT i.issue_key, i.lead_time_minutes AS ltm,
         COALESCE(MAX(w.status = 'assisted'), 0) AS ai
  FROM issues i
  JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = i.id
  LEFT JOIN commits gc
         ON gc.message REGEXP CONCAT('(^|[^A-Za-z0-9])', i.issue_key, '([^0-9]|$)')
  LEFT JOIN whodunit_commits w ON w.commit_sha = gc.sha
  WHERE bi.board_id = '$board'
    AND i.lead_time_minutes IS NOT NULL
    AND i.issue_key REGEXP '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+$'
  GROUP BY i.issue_key, i.lead_time_minutes
) t GROUP BY ai

defaults.noValue: no issues with a lead time on this board

panels.description:
Scoped to one board on purpose. Pooled across boards this comparison inverts — one board contributes 148 fast unassisted issues that drag the average down, so assisted looks 2.5x slower while being faster within every board taken separately. That is a mix artifact, not an AI effect.

Read it as a description of which work was chosen at least as much as what the agent did: harder issues get handed to an agent.

Issues are matched to commits by finding the key in the commit message, which is a text match rather than a recorded link.

options.content:
### Stages 5 and 6 cannot be measured here

**5 · Productivity — output per unit of effort.** Needs a pre-adoption baseline to compare against. None was captured on this machine, and that window closed when the hooks were installed. `dun baseline capture` records one for *future* comparisons; it cannot recover the past.

**6 · Business value — capacity unlocked in currency.** Depends on stage 5, plus a loaded engineering cost that whodunit does not hold and should not guess.

These stages are left empty rather than estimated. A productivity percentage computed without a baseline would be arithmetic on an assumption, and it would be the number people quoted.

`dun delta` reports the within-period comparison that *is* available, and prints its own warnings about thin data and the missing baseline.
